claims.text: The trace measures 15.52 km against a booked optimal route of 11.2 km: an excess of 4.32 km, or 38.57% of the optimal distance. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate are cleared on this trip's own measurement — the excess is greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal — so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED. The governing figure is the trace distance of 15.52 km, not the rounded 15.5 km convenience copy carried on the trip record, which POL-RD-01 forbids citing for the threshold test.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip identifier TRP-02803 is identical across the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix at 16:05:14 matches the recorded trip start at 16:05:14. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 122 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so it does not meet limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 and no independent corroboration of the deviation is required. The burden therefore shifts to the driver.

The driver's explanation — 'Traffic was heavy so I took another road' — names no evidence ID, and no traffic advisory for this trip is on file: EV-ADVIS-02803-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, which I disclose rather than present as clean. Under POL-RD-13 an asserted external traffic cause is tested against the traffic advisory and nothing else; with no advisory covering the trip window, POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight against the rider's proof under POL-RD-08. Because the driver cites no advisory identifier at all, the absent artifact is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire and the case does not escalate on this ground: the excess stands at the measured figure.

No part of the excess is attributable to a rider instruction. The chat log for this trip contains zero messages, so no request exists that could satisfy POL-RD-04(a) to (c), and there is no waypoint_hint and no named road for the trace to corroborate — POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and the excess is not reduced by a single metre before the threshold test. POL-RD-14 is not even reached: there is no instruction to find uncorroborated.

The baseline cannot be re-cut in the driver's favour. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 has no amended optimal for POL-RD-01 to be re-applied against, and the booked optimal of 11.2 km stands as the correct baseline for the excess.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier carried on the fare breakdown (the trip record does not carry the field) is 1.5, so recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 11.2 + 0.28 x 15.1) x 1.5 + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 ERP on the optimal route = 27.442. Charged total is 34.44, so the refund is 34.44 - 27.442 = 6.998, rounded up to SGD 7.00. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 20.3% of the charged total, far below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 7.00 — comfortably within the SGD 8.00 contested in this dispute — and no more.

The single ERP line — CTE Braddell southbound, SGD 2.00 — is matched to the trace: the nearest fix is 7.52 m from the gantry, well inside the 250 m crossing radius, and the fare breakdown records the gantry as lying on the optimal route. It is therefore already comprehended in the recomputed fare and must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure under POL-RD-09(1). There is no off-route and no phantom gantry here, so no separate pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(4) arises and the rider does not ask for one.

Nothing on the rider's profile bars or burdens this claim. The enhanced-corroboration trigger in POL-RD-08 requires rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d of 4 or more together with 1 or fewer substantiated; this rider stands at 1 claim and 0 substantiated, so the trigger does not fire and the ordinary standard applies — and the claim is proven on this trip's trace in any event. The rider profile is credibility context only under POL-GEN-01 and may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

The disputed charge is live and unreversed: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0. The rider is both the filing party and the party who paid, so a partial refund returns part of the contested amount to the rider under POL-GEN-03 and the rider stops carrying the 4.32 km of distance he was billed for and never travelled.

claims.text: The GPS trace governs the measurement, and what it shows is an established deviation that is not a material one. The trace records 15.52 km between the pickup fix at 16:05:14 and the dropoff fix at 16:25:24 against a booked optimal of 11.2 km: an excess of 4.32 km, or 38.57%. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment tests pass (excess above 20% and above 0.8 km), but neither materiality test is met (the excess is not above 50% and not above 8.0 km), so no material deviation is recorded and POL-RD-06's profile check, its full-refund uplift and its conduct referral are not engaged. The trip record's rounded 15.5 km copy is not the field the threshold test runs on; the trace figure is, and on the trace figure the case is a quantum dispute, not a conduct one.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be built against this driver. His profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 413 in the same trailing window, a ratio of 0.00 — far below the 0.05 the clause requires at a minimum of 40 completed trips. With no pattern established, POL-RD-06 licenses neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor a referral for driver-conduct review, and limb (a) does not rescue the rider either, because the evidence is not finely balanced: the excess is measured on a complete trace, not contested between two admissible accounts. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter on the same profile is a different field from the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names, and substituting it is forbidden by POL-GEN-01.

The refund is arithmetic, and it is smaller than the sum the rider contests. Running POL-RD-02 on the surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown (1.5, read from that artifact and not from the trip record): ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 11.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 15.1 optimal minutes) x 1.5) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 ERP on the optimal route = 27.4420. Charged_total of 34.44 less 27.4420 gives 6.9980 before rounding, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 7.00. That is 7.00 against the 8.00 claimed, and 20.3% of charged_total — nowhere near the 90% share that would make it a full refund, and above the 0.50 de minimis floor only marginally.

On the driver's side of that arithmetic, the recomputation leaves every legitimate line of the trip standing: the 1.5 surge multiplier carried on the fare breakdown is applied to base fare, distance charge and time charge; the 0.80 platform fee is retained; and the 2.00 of ERP sitting on the optimal route is passed through in full. What the formula strips out is only the distance and time the detour added — 4.32 km and roughly 5 minutes of meter — so no charge the rider actually consumed is returned to him.

The one pass-through line in this fare is properly the rider's, so no separate correction is owed on it. The only gantry charged is 'CTE Braddell southbound' at SGD 2.00; the fare breakdown flags it on_optimal_route true and the trace passes within 7.52 m of it at fix 14, well inside the 250 m matching rule. The off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry, no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding and no referral, and no standalone pass-through refund under POL-RD-09(2), because this deviation is not exonerated as an external event.

The driver's explanation — heavy traffic, another road — is not put forward as an exoneration, because it cannot be run on this record. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02803-01, is MISSING: it carries no payload and an admissibility weight_multiplier of 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03's first requirement, an advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the passage, cannot be satisfied at all, and under POL-RD-08 the assertion discharges nothing. As POL-RD-13 provides, that assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal, so the excess stands at 4.32 km and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked 11.2 km optimal route — the figure already used in the arithmetic above.

Both parties largely agree on the arithmetic, and the record supports it. The measured deviation is established but not material. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02803 records 15.52 km between the pickup fix (16:05:14) and the dropoff fix (16:25:24) against the booked optimal route of 11.2 km on EV-TRIP-02803 — an excess of 4.32 km, or 38.57% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (above 0.8 km and above 20%), but neither materiality test does (not above 50%, not above 8.0 km), so no material deviation is recorded. The governing figure is the trace distance of 15.52 km; the trip record's rounded 15.5 km copy is not used for the threshold test, and the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (122 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps), so no independent corroboration of the deviation was needed.

The driver's explanation — 'traffic was heavy so I took another road' — carries no weight. Under POL-RD-13 an asserted external traffic cause is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02803-01, is MISSING: it has no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. No advisory covers the trip window, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. Because the driver named no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire and the case does not escalate; the excess stands at the measured 4.32 km.

No part of the excess is rider-caused. The chat log EV-CHAT-02803 contains zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no instruction to test and no waypoint to corroborate, and POL-RD-14 is not reached. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 gives no amended optimal and the booked 11.2 km stands as the baseline.

Refund arithmetic under POL-RD-02 (fare model METERED; the surge multiplier of 1.5 is read from the fare breakdown EV-FARE-02803, which is the only artifact carrying it): recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 11.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 15.1 optimal min) x 1.5 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 ERP on the optimal route = 27.4420. Charged_total is 34.44, so the refund is 34.44 - 27.4420 = 6.9980, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 7.00. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 20.3% of charged_total, below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 7.00. Every legitimate line stands: base, distance, time and the 1.5 surge, the platform fee and the on-route ERP; only the distance and time the detour added are stripped out.

The single ERP line ('CTE Braddell southbound', SGD 2.00) is matched to the trace — the nearest fix is 7.52 m away, well inside the 250 m crossing radius — and the fare breakdown records it on the optimal route. It is already comprehended in the recomputed fare and is not added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). There is no off-route and no phantom gantry, so no standalone pass-through correction and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists: EV-DPROF-02803 shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 413, far below the POL-RD-06 ratio of 0.05, and the deviation is not material in any event. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter mentioned on the same profile is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not used for the test.

No driver compensation is due: the billed distance of 15.5 km falls short of the 15.52 km trace by only 0.02 km, below the 1.0 km shortfall POL-RD-04 requires. The rider profile is credibility context only and does not bar or burden the claim. The contested amount is live and unreversed (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), so the partial refund returns SGD 7.00 of the SGD 8.00 contested to the rider. The monetary effect does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 the refund executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the fare for TRP-02803 is recomputed and part of it is returned to the rider.

Measurement (POL-RD-01). The threshold test runs on the GPS trace, not the trip record's rounded copy. EV-GPS-02803 (weight 1.0; 122 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, longest gap 0.0 s) measures 15.52 km against the booked optimal of 11.2 km (EV-TRIP-02803): an excess of 4.32 km, or 38.57%. Both establishment tests pass — over 20% and over 0.8 km — so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. Neither materiality test is met (not over 50%, not over 8.0 km), so it is not MATERIAL; POL-RD-06's profile check (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 413 completed trips in the same 90-day window) finds no repeat pattern, and no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral are licensed.

His profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 413 in the same trailing window, a ratio of 0.00 — far below the 0.05 the clause requires at a minimum of 40 completed trips. With no pattern established, POL-RD-06 licenses neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor a referral for driver-conduct review, and limb (a) does not rescue the rider either, because the evidence is not finely balanced: the excess is measured on a complete trace, not contested between two admissible accounts. ledger.claim: The refund is arithmetic, and it is smaller than the sum the rider contests. Running POL-RD-02 on the surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown (1.5, read from that artifact and not from the trip record): ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 11.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 15.1 optimal minutes) x 1.5) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 ERP on the optimal route = 27.4420. Charged_total of 34.44 less 27.4420 gives 6.9980 before rounding, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 7.00. That is 7.00 against the 8.00 claimed, and 20.3% of charged_total — nowhere near the 90% share that would make it a full refund, and above the 0.50 de minimis floor only marginally.

On the driver's side of that arithmetic, the recomputation leaves every legitimate line of the trip standing: the 1.5 surge multiplier carried on the fare breakdown is applied to base fare, distance charge and time charge; the 0.80 platform fee is retained; and the 2.00 of ERP sitting on the optimal route is passed through in full. What the formula strips out is only the distance and time the detour added — 4.32 km and roughly 5 minutes of meter — so no charge the rider actually consumed is returned to him.

The one pass-through line in this fare is properly the rider's, so no separate correction is owed on it. The only gantry charged is 'CTE Braddell southbound' at SGD 2.00; the fare breakdown flags it on_optimal_route true and the trace passes within 7.52 m of it at fix 14, well inside the 250 m matching rule. The off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry, no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding and no referral, and no standalone pass-through refund under POL-RD-09(2), because this deviation is not exonerated as an external event.

The driver's explanation — heavy traffic, another road — is not put forward as an exoneration, because it cannot be run on this record. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02803-01, is MISSING: it carries no payload and an admissibility weight_multiplier of 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03's first requirement, an advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the passage, cannot be satisfied at all, and under POL-RD-08 the assertion discharges nothing. As POL-RD-13 provides, that assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal, so the excess stands at 4.32 km and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked 11.2 km optimal route — the figure already used in the arithmetic above.
